skill.name: plugin-settings
skill.description: Guides plugin authors through storing per-project settings in .claude/*.local.md files using YAML frontmatter and Markdown body content. Includes examples for reading, validating, creating, and documenting local plugin configuration in hooks, commands, and agents.
skill.summary: Document a local settings pattern for configurable Claude Code plugins.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Static findings were mostly false positives from Markdown code fences, Bash examples, validation messages, and defensive path checks. No explicit prompt injection attempt, credential exfiltration, network access, or malicious command execution was found. One semantic concern remains: examples show local Markdown body text being reused as prompt or control-flow content.

remediation.issue: Local Markdown body content can be reused as agent prompt text.
remediation.suggestion: Treat .claude/*.local.md body content as project input, not trusted instruction. Require user intent before feeding it back into agent control flow.

remediation.issue: Shell parsing examples are suitable only for simple settings.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend strict schemas and a YAML parser for complex fields. Keep grep and sed examples limited to simple scalar values.

remediation.issue: Local settings files may contain private project state.
remediation.suggestion: Emphasize gitignore rules, user-only permissions, and avoiding secrets in every setup and README example.

content.value_statement: Plugin authors need a safe way to store per-project settings without committing user-specific state. This skill explains a local Markdown and YAML frontmatter pattern for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plugins.
actual_capabilities: Show YAML frontmatter templates for booleans, strings, numbers, lists, and Markdown notes.
Demonstrate Bash hook parsing with defaults, validation, and disabled-mode exits.
Provide guidance for command-based setup flows using user preference questions.
Document gitignore, permissions, restart, and atomic update practices.
limitations: It is documentation and examples; it does not install or enforce settings automatically.
Shell parsing examples are best for simple fields, not complex YAML structures.
Settings changes still require a Claude Code restart for hook behavior.
Prompt-bearing Markdown body content must be trusted before reuse.

best_practices: Keep settings project-local, user-managed, and excluded from version control.
Validate every setting before using it in hooks, commands, or agents.
Document restart requirements and provide safe defaults when the file is absent.
anti_patterns: Treating Markdown body text as trusted system instructions.
Using shell parsing for complex nested YAML without validation.
Storing secrets or shared team policy in local settings files.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It shows plugin authors how to store per-project plugin settings in a local Markdown file with YAML frontmatter.

faq.question: Does it create settings files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, examples, and command guidance that plugin authors can adapt.

faq.question: Why use .local.md files?
faq.answer: They are readable by users, easy to edit, and intended for local state that should not be committed.

faq.question: Can settings be read from hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show hooks reading frontmatter, applying defaults, and exiting cleanly when disabled.

faq.question: Are the Bash examples safe for all YAML?
faq.answer: No. They work best for simple scalar fields. Complex YAML should use a proper parser and schema validation.

faq.question: Should settings files contain secrets?
faq.answer: No. Settings files should not store credentials, tokens, or private data that belongs in a secret manager.
